title: Proper signed-word colimits attach alternating words along their boundaries
statement:
Let $\mathcal I$ be the category [def-nagata-category] of finite words in $+,-$, including the empty word $\epsilon$, with morphisms the weakly order-preserving maps of letter positions preserving signs. Composition is composition of maps of positions. For $n\geq0$ let $\mathcal I_{\leq n}$ be its full subcategory of words of length at most $n$. Let $E:\mathcal I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be a functor to simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Assume $E$ is proper: every injective morphism $u$ induces a degreewise injective $E(u)$, and, for any two injections into the same word, the intersection of their image simplicial subsets is exactly the image of the injection of their common positions. Put $C_n(E)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal I_{\leq n}}E$, with colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $n\geq1$ let $a_n^+$ and $a_n^-$ be the length-$n$ alternating words starting with $+$ and $-$, respectively. For $e\in\{+,-\}$ let $B_n^e(E)\subseteq E(a_n^e)$ be the union of the images of $E(u)$ for all injections $u:w\hookrightarrow a_n^e$ with $|w|<n$, including $w=\epsilon$. The prescriptions sending $E(u)(x)$ to the image of $x\in E(w)$ in $C_{n-1}(E)$ define well-defined simplicial maps $B_n^e(E)\to C_{n-1}(E)$. For each $n\geq1$ the canonical square
$$\begin{matrix}
B_n^+(E)\amalg B_n^-(E)&\longrightarrow&C_{n-1}(E)\\
\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow\\
E(a_n^+)\amalg E(a_n^-)&\longrightarrow&C_n(E)
\end{matrix}$$
is a pushout, meaning that maps from its lower-right corner to any simplicial set are uniquely determined by maps from its upper-right and lower-left corners agreeing on its upper-left corner. The left map is the coproduct of the two boundary inclusions; the right and bottom maps are induced by the colimit cocones. The construction is natural for natural transformations between proper functors. At degree zero, $C_0(E)=E(\epsilon)$.

source.place: Section 4.1, Definition 4.1 (indexing words), Proposition 4.3 (displayed attachment square), and Definition 4.4 (properness), printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7). Proper-functor version, with n >= 1 and degree zero treated separately; coproducts replace the displayed disjoint-union symbols.

proof.text: Every morphism f:w→v factors as p:w→m followed by i:m↪v, where m is the word on the ordered image of the position map, p is surjective, and i is the inclusion of that image. The signs are inherited from v and agree with those of w. Every fiber of a monotone map is an interval. Thus, if w is alternating, no fiber can contain two positions: it would also contain an adjacent pair of opposite signs. Every morphism with alternating source is therefore injective; if source and target have length n it is the order bijection, hence the identity of the same signed word.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: Let r(w) be the word obtained by replacing each maximal consecutive run of one sign by one letter, and let q_w:w→r(w) send each position to its run index (q_ε is the identity). If w is a nonalternating length-n word, |r(w)|<n. For any sign-preserving monotone surjection p:w→m, each target position has a nonempty interval fiber of its own sign. Expanding these fibers neither changes the ordered list of runs nor their signs. Consequently r(w)=r(m) as signed words and q_m∘p=q_w.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: For two proper injections u:w↪a_n^e and v:w′↪a_n^e, let h:t↪a_n^e be their common-position injection, with h=u∘u′=v∘v′. If E(u)(x)=E(v)(y), the intersection hypothesis supplies z∈E(t) in the same simplicial degree with this common value equal to E(h)(z). Injectivity of E(u) and E(v) gives x=E(u′)(z) and y=E(v′)(z). All three words w,w′,t have length less than n, so their lower-colimit cocone maps κ satisfy κ_w(x)=κ_t(z)=κ_w′(y). This proves independence of representatives for b_e:B_n^e(E)→C_{n-1}(E). Each subword image is stable under simplicial operators, and on it b_e E(u)=κ_w; applying an operator to this identity shows b_e commutes with every operator. Thus the union is a simplicial subset and b_e is a simplicial map. Empty intersections are covered by t=ε and the stated properness hypothesis.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: Fix a simplicial set T and compatible maps f:C_{n-1}(E)→T and g_e:E(a_n^e)→T with g_e|_{B_n^e}=f b_e. For each |w|≤n define a simplicial map h_w:E(w)→T: put h_w=f κ_w if |w|<n, put h_w=g_e for w=a_n^e, and put h_w=f κ_{r(w)} E(q_w) for a nonalternating length-n word. The latter is defined because |r(w)|<n. Each formula is a composite of simplicial maps.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: Check first every arrow j:m→v with |m|<n. If |v|<n, the lower-colimit cocone identity gives h_v E(j)=h_m. If v is nonalternating of length n, both m and r(v) lie in the lower category, so κ_{r(v)} E(q_v∘j)=κ_m and again h_v E(j)=h_m. If v=a_n^e, factor j=i p through its ordered image t. Since |t|≤|m|<n, the image of E(i) lies in B_n^e. Therefore g_e E(i)E(p)=f κ_t E(p)=f κ_m=h_m, as required.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: Now let p:w→m be a surjection with |w|=n and |m|<n. Its source cannot be alternating by Step 1. Step 2 gives r(w)=r(m) and q_w=q_m∘p. Since m and r(m) are in the lower category, κ_{r(m)} E(q_m)=κ_m. Thus h_w=f κ_{r(w)} E(q_w)=f κ_m E(p)=h_m E(p). This explicitly proves compatibility with every collapse, including different collapses of the same run.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: For an arbitrary arrow j:w→v with |w|=n and |v|≤n, an injective j must be the identity, because its target has at most n positions. Otherwise its ordered image t has length less than n, and j=i p with p:w→t surjective and i:t↪v. Step 6 gives h_w=h_t E(p); Step 5 gives h_t=h_v E(i). Hence h_w=h_v E(j). Together with Step 5 this checks every arrow of the truncated category, including nonidentity endomorphisms of nonalternating words. The family (h_w) is therefore a simplicial cocone and induces H:C_n(E)→T by the colimit universal property.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: The square commutes: on E(u)(x) in either boundary, the two routes to C_n(E) agree by its cocone identity, and Step 3 makes the upper map well defined. The H of Step 7 restricts to f on C_{n-1}(E) (check all its cocone components) and to g_e on the alternating values. Conversely, a map out of C_n(E) restricts to compatible f,g_+,g_-. These restrictions determine every cocone component: the lower ones by f, the alternating top ones by g_e, and each nonalternating top one by the arrow q_w to r(w) and the cocone identity. Colimit uniqueness then determines the map out of C_n(E). This proves exactly the displayed pushout universal property in simplicial sets, without using an additional assertion about pointwise computation of colimits.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: For a natural transformation η:E⇒E′ between proper functors, naturality on each subword injection gives η_{a_n^e} E(u)=E′(u)η_w, so η_{a_n^e} maps B_n^e(E) into B_n^e(E′). On a representative E(u)(x), both composites from B_n^e(E) to C_{n-1}(E′) equal κ′_w η_w(x), proving compatibility with b_e. The components η_w induce the truncated-colimit maps by the colimit universal property; their defining identities also give compatibility with the bottom and right maps. Hence η induces a morphism of the attachment squares, compatible with composition and identities by the same component identities. No injectivity of η is needed.

source.place: Section 4, indexing category 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); elementary details supplied here.

proof.text: When n=0 the only word is ε, and its only position map is the identity of the empty set. A cocone on this one-object identity diagram is exactly a simplicial map out of E(ε). Thus E(ε) has the universal property of C_0(E), giving the stated canonical identification.
